correctness.rationale: I independently enumerated all \(2^{10}=1024\) labeled tournaments on five alternatives and recomputed both solution concepts from their definitions. The Banks set was obtained from inclusion-maximal transitive subtournaments, with transitivity checked by absence of directed 3-cycles; the minimal covering set was obtained by direct external covering-stability testing. This reproduced the exact order-five histogram \((1,1):320,(3,3):520,(5,5):64,(4,3):120\), with exactly 120 disparities, all satisfying \(MC(T)\subsetneq BA(T)\). Canonicalization under all \(5!\) relabelings gave one canonical code, occurring 120 times, hence one asymmetric isomorphism class with full orbit size 120. This independently verifies the package's finite classification rather than relying on its saved output.
risks: The theorem is only the complete first disparity layer at order five; it does not classify higher-order tournament disparities.

originality.rationale: The 2015 disparity paper was inspected in an author-hosted full PDF. It reports exhaustive generation of non-isomorphic tournaments through order ten, gives disparity index five for Banks versus minimal covering, and displays a five-alternative witness with the 4-versus-3 choice sets. Those published statements establish the threshold and a witness but do not state that every order-five disparity is the same isomorphism class, nor the labeled count 120 and probability 15/128. Resultary and targeted exact searches did not locate a published uniqueness/census theorem. Thus the threshold is prior work, while the complete threshold-layer classification survives as original to the best of current evidence.
residual_risks: The 2015 authors' underlying exhaustive data may already contain the same one-class census even though the inspected published statements do not report it.

value.rationale: The first order at which two standard tournament solutions separate is a natural structural boundary. Classifying every tournament on that first layer, rather than merely exhibiting a witness, shows that the discrepancy has a unique symmetry type and a fixed containment pattern. That complete minimal-layer classification is mathematically useful and not an arbitrary finite slice.
risks: No claim is made about order six or asymptotic disparity frequencies.

limitations: The order-five threshold and existence witness are explicitly treated as prior work.
Originality is best-of-knowledge; unpublished enumeration data remain a residual risk.
